title: RPC call validation / probe log
content:
Context:
- Quick personal log while chasing a recurring parsing/validation bug for function/tool calls when responses are streamed from the hosted runtime. Seen in customer repros and internal fuzzing harnesses.
- Symptoms: occasional JSON parse errors in consumer SDKs (JS/TS SDKs primarily). The model output looks like valid fn-call JSON in logs, but SDKs throw SyntaxError when JSON.parse is invoked on the final chunk.

Incident summary (observed):
1) User request triggers a function-call response from model. We stream tokens back as text event chunks (newline-delimited).
2) On ~1–3% of requests in stress/fuzz tests, the assembled string (concatenation of chunks) fails JSON.parse with messages like `Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 1023` or `Unexpected end of JSON input` depending on timing.
3) In internal debug logs the model output string (printed raw) *looks* fine — matching braces, quoting OK. However, binary trace of the streamed bytes reveals trailing NULs or stray control characters in some cases.

Commands and probes tried (notes + commands I ran):
- Repro harness: python scripts/local_fuzz_harness.py --seed 20251102 --workers 20 --duration 60m
- Curl to dev edge + capture raw bytes:
  curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer dev-token" \n    -X POST https://edge.dev.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate \n    --data-binary @payload.json -o /tmp/resp.raw
- Inspect hex and control chars: hexdump -C /tmp/resp.raw | sed -n '1,200p'
- Convert to Python bytes and print repr() to highlight control chars: python - <<'PY'
import sys, pathlib
b=pathlib.Path('/tmp/resp.raw').read_bytes()
print(repr(b[:1200]))
PY
- Local sdk test (node): node test/stream-parser-smoke.js --logRaw > /tmp/sdk.raw
- Diff raw server vs sdk capture: cmp -l /tmp/resp.raw /tmp/sdk.raw | head

Findings so far:
- When request uses bursty tokens (long initial text then immediate fn-call JSON), the server HTTP/2 framing occasionally pads or sends a stream frame where the last payload has a 0x00 byte appended (not visible when printing as text in many consoles).
- The NULs correlate with certain sequence lengths. Re-running same seed sometimes reproduces; sometimes not. Points to either non-deterministic buffering path or race.
- The SDK's streaming consumer concatenates chunk.toString('utf8') then JSON.parse at end — which fails when NULs exist. Printing to a terminal hides NULs unless explicitly hex-dumped.
- Not a model tokenization issue for majority: the model's plain text output (as captured from runtime's internal emitter before HTTP framing) is valid JSON. The corruption seems to occur in the transport or the wrapper that re-encodes events into HTTP/2 frames for streaming.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Buffer reuse bug in streaming encoder: a `Buffer` used for frame payloads is allocated larger than payload and not properly sliced; leftover bytes from previous frames (NULs or older data) appended to last frame when chunk length < buffer length. (High probability)
2) OR TLS encryption block padding edge case when chunk length % cipherBlockSize == 0; decrypted output includes padding bytes misinterpreted by downstream reader. (Medium)
3) Race in chunk assembly: end-of-stream marker emission overlaps with flush() causing partial frame + stray zero bytes. (Low-Medium)
4) Model outputs invisible control chars due to token decoding (unlikely given internal pre-send logs). (Low)

Quick source-code grep targets (where to look):
- runtime/http2/streaming-encoder.js (suspect Buffer allocation / copy logic)
- runtime/edge-proxy/frame-writer.ts (frame builder)
- node http2 core shim in edge binary (C++ layer) if Buffer reuse present there

Repro experiments to run next (planned):
- Narrow down with deterministic small inputs: create a payload that triggers a 512-byte exact JSON output and another that triggers 513 bytes to see boundary behavior. Use Python harness to vary output lengths by 1 byte.
- Add Canary instrumentation: before sending frame, log (hex) the last 64 bytes of the payload and after send, verify what arrived at consumer (hex). Add XOR checksum per-frame to detect silent mutations.
- Add `Buffer.alloc(payloadLength)` instead of `Buffer.allocUnsafe` in suspected paths to check if zeroing avoids error. (If bug goes away -> buffer reuse).
- Run with openssl debug on TLS to eliminate padding theory.
- Turn on `--trace-gc` on node workers to see if GC compaction correlates (weird but sometimes reveals reuse).

Interim mitigation for SDKs / clients:
- Defensive JSON cleaning in SDK: trim trailing NULs and control chars before JSON.parse (quick patch). Example: str = str.replace(/\u0000+$/g, ''); BUT this masks root cause and might hide further corruption.
- Add final validation: if parse fails, attempt hex-dump of bytes and fail loudly with diagnostic data uploaded to a debug bucket (avoid PII).

Observed error snippets (copied raw):
- Node consumer stack: SyntaxError: Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 1023
  at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
  at StreamParser.finalize (/home/jordan/workspace/sdk/src/stream-parser.js:214:27)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)

- Hex snippet from corrupted resp.raw (showing trailing 00):
  00000400  7d 22 2c 20 22 69 64 22  3a 22 61 62 63 64 22 7d  |}, "id":"abcd"}|
  00000410  00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  00 00 00 00               |............|

- Internal pre-send log (runtime emitter):
  EMIT: {"name":"create_item","arguments":{"title":"test","id":"abcd"}}
  (no trailing NULs visible here)

Notes on test harness and fuzzing approach used: 
- Harness is schema-driven: we feed model deterministic fn-call schemas and use a tiny local model stub that returns the JSON structure exactly to isolate transport corruption. The stub returns a strict single-line JSON string.
- Fuzzer mutates the ordering of fields and injects optional unicode characters to stress serialization. This surfaced a separate bug where control chars in text fields were not escaped consistently, but that's a different thread.

Debug artifacts saved: (local)
- /tmp/stream-corrupt-20251103/resp-*.raw (raw bytes captured)
- /tmp/stream-corrupt-20251103/sdk-*.log (node sdk captures)
- gist drafts with sample corrupted hex: https://gist.github.com/jordanlee/stream-corrupt-samples (internal)

Next steps (actionable short list):
- [ ] Add small deterministic unit test that writes frames with payload lengths 1..1024 and asserts consumer receives identical bytes. Place test in runtime/http2/tests/frame-roundtrip.spec.ts.
- [ ] Patch suspect allocator points from allocUnsafe -> alloc to confirm behavior; run fuzz for 12h.
- [ ] Instrument frame writer to log last 32 bytes (hex) for high-latency/failing requests and route logs to debug index.
- [ ] If alloc fixes, propose PR to runtime repo and schedule quick rollback window on staging; coordinate with SRE for canary.
- [ ] Prepare SDK quick-fix: on parse failure, dump hex snapshot + fail with a more helpful error linking to the debug ID. Roll as patchrelease to node clients.

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Could any edge load-balancer TCP proxy be rewriting frames (unlikely but need to verify path for customers seeing this)? Which LB versions are in front of affected customers?
- Are there particular model sizes or response shapes that correlate? Need more telemetry on sequence lengths for each failing request.
- Validate if this appears on Dedicated / Private (customer reported on hosted). If not present in Private, helps isolate to hosted edge binary.

Notes to self (fragments):
- If buffer reuse, likely introduced during refactor 2025-06 where frame writer switched to pooling for perf. Check commit range 2025-06..2025-08 in runtime repo.
- Try running fuzz with `NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-gc --expose-gc` to push GC behavior.

Bottom line (current working theory):
- Most likely a buffer reuse / allocUnsafe path causing stale bytes (NULs or earlier data) to survive in the final frame. Prioritize adding deterministic tests and switching to safer alloc for suspected code paths to validate.

If I can't reproduce within next 24h with alloc tweak, escalate to edge binary owners (Samir) and request an instrumented canary of frame_writer binary with extra sanity checks.
